# Configuration reference

bb-box's configuration is one document (029): `bb box config show --json` prints it, and `bb box config apply <file>` saves one. BB Box's settings page edits the same document. A secret field reads `{ "set": true }` in an export, and takes a string to set it.

## The document

| Key | Type | Default | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `schema` | `typeof SCHEMA` |  | The document's format: 1. |
| `revision` | `number` |  | Counts each save. A file applied with a revision is refused when the configuration has changed since. |
| `backends` | `readonly BackendConfig[]` |  | In the order the registry tries them. |
| `kinds` | `Readonly<Record<string, KindConfig>>` |  | Each kind's entry, by its ID: only what differs from its defaults. |
| `general` | `GeneralSettings` |  | Settings for every backend and kind. |
| `images` | `Readonly<Record<string, ImageConfig>>` |  | Projects' images, by name (049). |

## general

| Key | Type | Default | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `boxesPerThread` | `number` | `0` | The most boxes a thread may hold at once. 0 means no limit. |
| `enrol` | `boolean` | `true` | Whether boxes join BB as machines, so threads and terminals can use them with the thread's credentials. |
| `defaultKind` | `string` | `"linux"` | The kind a thread gets when it asks for none. |
| `files` | `readonly BoxFileSetting[]` |  | Files for every box (#455): paths under the box user's home, whose contents are secrets. |
| `video` | `boolean` | `false` | Whether a viewer of a Linux X11 desktop on the CPU may show it as video, through Selkies (056): when its round trip to BB's server is slow, or when the viewer chose it. Off while it is tried. |

## kinds

Each kind's entry, by its ID. A kind with no entry has its defaults, in the [kinds reference](kinds.md). A kind keeps at most 10 spares.

| Key | Type | Default | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | `boolean` |  | Off, no backend offers new boxes of the kind. On when left out. |
| `presets` | `Partial<Readonly<Record<Preset, SizeChange>>>` |  | Changes to the small, medium and large sizes: cores, memoryGiB and diskGiB, each optional. |
| `default` | `Preset` |  | The preset a box gets when it asks for no size. |
| `largest` | `SizeChange` |  | The most a custom size may ask for, as a size change. |
| `spares` | `number` |  | Spare boxes to keep: ready, enrolled and owned by no thread (032). |

## backends

Each backend's entry, in the order acquire tries them. Its ID is its type, or `<type>:<name>` for another backend of the type. A backend keeps at most 20 warm boxes of a kind.

| Key | Type | Default | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` |  | The type, or "<type>:<name>" for another backend of the type. |
| `type` | `string` |  | The driver. |
| `label` | `string` |  | Display name. The driver's label when left out. |
| `enabled` | `boolean` |  | Off, the backend takes no new boxes; its boxes keep working. |
| `fields` | `Readonly<Record<string, FieldValue \| SecretState>>` |  | What the operator set. Stored without secrets; shown with each as its state. |
| `warm` | `Readonly<Record<string, number>>` |  | Ready guests to keep, by kind. |
| `hosts` | `readonly HostConfig[]` |  | For a driver with host fields. |

A host of a backend with hosts:

| Key | Type | Default | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` |  | Lower-case letters, digits and "-", unique in its backend. |
| `enabled` | `boolean` |  | Off, the host takes no new boxes; its boxes keep working. |
| `fields` | `Readonly<Record<string, FieldValue>>` |  | The host's own fields, as its driver lists them. |

## images

Projects' images, by name (049).

| Key | Type | Default | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kinds` | `readonly string[]` |  | The kinds it builds on, such as linux and linux-desktop-cpu. |
| `script` | `string` |  | The script, run as root in a box of the kind's standard image. |
| `check` | `string` |  | Run as the box user after the script: the image fails when it fails. |
| `bake` | `ImageBake` |  | When it is built ahead: auto, after two boxes in 14 days; always; or never, so it runs at each start. |
| `projects` | `readonly string[]` |  | The BB projects whose threads' boxes get it. |
| `source` | `{ readonly script?: string; readonly check?: string }` |  | Where the files came from in the project's repository, such as .bb/box-setup.sh. |
| `updated` | `string` |  | When it was set, as an ISO 8601 time. |

## Each backend's fields

| Type | Backend | Kinds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`proxmox-lxc`](#proxmox-lxc) | Proxmox LXC | linux, linux-desktop, linux-desktop-cpu, linux-desktop-wayland-cpu |
| [`proxmox-qemu`](#proxmox-qemu) | Proxmox QEMU | windows-desktop |
| [`ssh-pool`](#ssh-pool) | SSH host pool | linux, macos, macos-desktop |
| [`tart`](#tart) | Tart | macos, macos-desktop, linux-arm64, linux-arm64-desktop-cpu, windows-arm64-desktop |
| [`docker`](#docker) | Docker | linux, linux-desktop-cpu, linux-desktop, linux-desktop-wayland-cpu |
| [`microsandbox`](#microsandbox) | microsandbox | linux, linux-desktop-cpu, linux-arm64, linux-arm64-desktop-cpu |

### proxmox-lxc

Proxmox LXC: Linux boxes, with or without a desktop, as containers on a Proxmox VE host.

Setup: [setup/proxmox-lxc/README.md](../../setup/proxmox-lxc/README.md).

| Field | Label | Type | Group | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `url` | API URL | string | connection |  | For example https://192.0.2.10:8006/api2/json, as the setup guide's token file gives it. |
| `node` | Node | string | connection |  | The node boxes run on. Leave empty on a single-node host. |
| `tls-fingerprint` | TLS fingerprint | string | connection |  | The SHA-256 fingerprint of the Proxmox API's certificate, from the setup guide's token file. bb-box then trusts that certificate alone. Leave empty to check the certificate against its CA. |
| `ca-certificate` | CA certificate | string | connection |  | PEM certificate of the CA that signed the Proxmox API's certificate, when there is no TLS fingerprint. Leave empty for a publicly trusted one. |
| `token-id` | API token ID | string | credentials |  | For example bbbox@pve!plugin. The setup guide lists the privileges it needs. |
| `token-secret` | API token secret | string, secret | credentials |  | The secret of the API token, from the setup guide's token file. |
| `ssh-private-key` | SSH private key | string, secret | credentials |  | The unencrypted OpenSSH private key the templates were built with (the setup guide's BBBOX_SSH_KEY). Leave empty and bb-box makes one and shows its public key, which the templates must then accept. |
| `pool` | Resource pool | string | boxes | `bbbox` | Boxes are made in this pool. The token needs rights on it. |
| `linux-templates` | Linux templates | string | boxes | `9100` | VMIDs of the CT templates linux boxes are linked clones of, separated by spaces or commas. Empty turns them off. |
| `desktop-templates` | GPU desktop templates | string | boxes |  | One line per GPU desktop template that linux-desktop boxes are linked clones of: its VMID, a space and the ID of the GPU it carries, such as the UUID nvidia-smi -L shows. Empty turns them off. |
| `desktop-cpu-templates` | CPU desktop templates | string | boxes |  | VMIDs of the CPU-only desktop templates linux-desktop-cpu boxes are linked clones of, separated by spaces or commas. Empty turns them off. |
| `desktop-wayland-cpu-templates` | CPU Wayland desktop templates | string | boxes |  | VMIDs of the CPU-only Wayland desktop templates linux-desktop-wayland-cpu boxes are linked clones of, separated by spaces or commas. Empty turns them off. |
| `desktops-per-gpu` | Desktops per GPU | number | advanced | `0` | A new linux-desktop box goes to the GPU with the fewest desktops, and is refused when every GPU runs this many. 0 means no limit. |
| `bridge` | Network bridge | string | advanced | `vmbr200` | The bridge boxes attach to. |
| `subnet` | Subnet | string | advanced | `10.200.0.0/24` | The bridge's subnet in CIDR form. Boxes get static addresses; there is no DHCP. |
| `gateway` | Gateway | string | advanced | `10.200.0.1` | The host's address on the bridge. |
| `addresses` | Box addresses | string | advanced | `10.200.0.10-10.200.0.254` | The range bb-box hands out. The n-th VMID gets the n-th address. Leave empty to use the whole subnet except the gateway. |
| `vmid-first` | First box VMID | number | advanced | `9900` | Boxes take VMIDs from this range. Keep other guests out of it. |
| `vmid-last` | Last box VMID | number | advanced | `9999` | The end of the range boxes take VMIDs from. |
| `ssh-user` | SSH user | string | advanced | `box` | The user in the templates that bb-box and BB work as. |
| `reserve-memory-mib` | Memory kept free (MiB) | number | advanced | `4096` | A new box is refused if the node would have less memory than this left. |
| `reserve-disk-gib` | Disk kept free (GiB) | number | advanced | `50` | A new box is refused if the template's storage has less free space than this. |

### proxmox-qemu

Proxmox QEMU: Windows desktops as VMs on a Proxmox VE host.

Setup: [setup/proxmox-qemu/README.md](../../setup/proxmox-qemu/README.md).

Fields left empty take proxmox-lxc's, a set at a time: `url`, `token-id`, `token-secret`, `tls-fingerprint`, `ca-certificate`; `ssh-private-key`.

| Field | Label | Type | Group | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `url` | API URL | string | connection |  | For example https://192.0.2.10:8006/api2/json, as the Proxmox LXC setup guide's token file gives it. Leave it, the token, the fingerprint and the CA certificate empty to use Proxmox LXC's. |
| `node` | Node | string | connection |  | The node boxes run on. Leave empty on a single-node host. |
| `tls-fingerprint` | TLS fingerprint | string | connection |  | The SHA-256 fingerprint of the Proxmox API's certificate, from the setup guide's token file. bb-box then trusts that certificate alone. Leave empty to check the certificate against its CA. |
| `ca-certificate` | CA certificate | string | connection |  | PEM certificate of the CA that signed the Proxmox API's certificate, when there is no TLS fingerprint. Leave empty for a publicly trusted one. |
| `token-id` | API token ID | string | credentials |  | For example bbbox@pve!plugin. The setup guide lists the privileges it needs. |
| `token-secret` | API token secret | string, secret | credentials |  | The secret of the API token, from the setup guide's token file. |
| `ssh-private-key` | SSH private key | string, secret | credentials |  | Paste BBBOX_SSH_KEY, the private key build.sh put in the template, or leave it empty to use Proxmox LXC's. With neither, bb-box makes a key, which the template does not accept until you add its public key. |
| `pool` | Resource pool | string | boxes | `bbbox` | Boxes are made in this pool. The token needs rights on it. |
| `windows-templates` | Windows templates | string | boxes | `9104` | VMIDs of the Windows templates windows-desktop boxes are linked clones of, separated by spaces or commas. setup/proxmox-qemu/build.sh builds one. A new box is cloned from the least used. |
| `windows-enrol` | Windows boxes as BB machines | boolean | boxes | `true` | Windows boxes join BB as machines, so threads and terminals can use them, as Linux and macOS boxes do. Off, they are boxes only. |
| `bridge` | Network bridge | string | advanced | `vmbr200` | The bridge boxes attach to. |
| `subnet` | Subnet | string | advanced | `10.200.0.0/24` | The bridge's subnet in CIDR form. Boxes get static addresses; there is no DHCP. |
| `gateway` | Gateway | string | advanced | `10.200.0.1` | The host's address on the bridge. |
| `addresses` | Box addresses | string | advanced | `10.200.0.150-10.200.0.254` | The range bb-box hands out. The n-th VMID gets the n-th address. Keep it apart from the Proxmox LXC backend's. Leave empty to use the whole subnet except the gateway. |
| `vmid-first` | First box VMID | number | advanced | `9700` | Boxes take VMIDs from this range. Keep other guests out of it, the Proxmox LXC backend's too. |
| `vmid-last` | Last box VMID | number | advanced | `9799` | The end of the range boxes take VMIDs from. |
| `ssh-user` | SSH user | string | advanced | `box` | The user in the template that bb-box and BB work as. |
| `reserve-memory-mib` | Memory kept free (MiB) | number | advanced | `4096` | A new box is refused if the node would have less memory than this left. |
| `reserve-disk-gib` | Disk kept free (GiB) | number | advanced | `50` | A new box is refused if the template's storage has less free space than this. |

### ssh-pool

SSH host pool: Your own Linux machines and Macs, reached over SSH and reset between boxes.

Setup: [setup/ssh-pool/README.md](../../setup/ssh-pool/README.md).

| Field | Label | Type | Group | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `machines` | Machines | string | boxes |  | One line per machine: a name, [user@]host[:port], its kinds, and optionally via=<jump host>, reset=machine and labels=<words>. For example "build-1 192.0.2.21 linux" or "mac-mini 192.0.2.30 macos,macos-desktop". setup/ssh-pool/setup.sh, or setup-mac.sh on a Mac, prints the line for each machine. |
| `known-hosts` | Host keys | string | connection |  | known_hosts lines for every machine and jump host, as setup.sh and setup-mac.sh print them. bb-box connects only to a machine whose key is here. |
| `ssh-private-key` | SSH private key | string, secret | credentials |  | An unencrypted OpenSSH private key that the machines' admin user accepts. Leave empty and bb-box makes one and shows its public key, which you then give setup.sh. |

### tart

Tart: macOS boxes, and Linux and Windows boxes on arm64, as VMs on your Macs with Apple silicon.

Setup: [setup/tart/README.md](../../setup/tart/README.md).

| Field | Label | Type | Group | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ssh-private-key` | SSH private key | string, secret | credentials |  | The unencrypted OpenSSH private key that each Mac's user and each image's VM user accept. Leave empty and bb-box makes one and shows its public key. |
| `macos-image` | macOS image | string | boxes | `bb-box-macos` | The Tart VM on each Mac that macos boxes, with no desktop shown, are cloned from. Empty turns them off. |
| `macos-desktop-image` | macOS desktop image | string | boxes | `bb-box-macos` | The Tart VM on each Mac that macos-desktop boxes are cloned from. Empty turns them off. |
| `linux-image` | Linux image (arm64) | string | boxes |  | The Tart VM on each Mac that linux-arm64 boxes are cloned from, as setup/tart/prepare-linux-image.sh builds it (bb-box-linux). Empty turns them off. |
| `linux-desktop-image` | Linux desktop image (arm64) | string | boxes |  | The Tart VM on each Mac that linux-arm64-desktop-cpu boxes are cloned from, as setup/tart/prepare-linux-image.sh --desktop builds it (bb-box-linux-desktop). Empty turns them off. |
| `windows-image` | Windows image (arm64) | string | boxes |  | The Windows image on each Mac, in ~/.bb-box/qemu/images, that windows-arm64-desktop boxes are made from, run by QEMU. Empty turns them off. |
| `windows-enrol` | Windows boxes as BB machines | boolean | boxes | `true` | Windows boxes join BB as machines, so threads and terminals can use them, as Linux and macOS boxes do. Off, they are boxes only. |
| `vm-user` | VM user | string | advanced | `admin` | The user in the macOS images that bb-box and BB work as. It is logged in to the desktop automatically. Linux boxes work as box. |
| `vms-per-host` | VMs per Mac | number | advanced | `2` | The most macOS VMs that run on each Mac at once, counting every VM Tart runs there, not only bb-box's. At most 2, which Apple's licence and the Virtualization framework allow. |
| `reserve-memory-mib` | Memory kept free (MiB) | number | advanced | `16384` | A new box is refused if the Mac would have less memory than this left for its own use, after its running VMs. |
| `reserve-disk-gib` | Disk kept free (GiB) | number | advanced | `50` | A new box is refused if the Mac's disk has less free space than this. |

Each host's fields:

| Field | Label | Type | Group | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `address` | Address | string | connection |  | The Mac's address, with :port when SSH is not on 22. For example 192.0.2.20. |
| `user` | User | string | connection |  | The user bb-box logs in to the Mac as, which runs tart. |
| `host-keys` | Host keys | string | connection |  | The Mac's SSH host keys as known_hosts lines. ssh-keyscan -t ed25519 <address> prints one. bb-box checks them on every connection. |

### docker

Docker: Linux boxes, with or without a desktop, as containers on a Docker host. It needs only Docker.

Setup: [setup/docker/README.md](../../setup/docker/README.md).

| Field | Label | Type | Group | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `host` | Host | string | connection |  | Where the Docker daemon is, as unix:///path/to/docker.sock, ssh://user@host, or bb:<machine ID> for a BB machine, which bb-box reaches through BB. Empty uses the docker CLI's own default on BB's server: DOCKER_HOST, its current context, or the local socket. Over SSH, BB's server user must log in without a prompt. |
| `linux-image` | Linux image | string | boxes | `bbbox/linux:1` | The image linux boxes run. setup/docker/build.sh builds it. Empty turns them off. |
| `desktop-image` | Desktop image | string | boxes | `bbbox/linux-desktop:1` | The image linux-desktop-cpu boxes, and linux-desktop boxes when GPU desktops are on, run. setup/docker/build.sh builds it. Empty turns them off. |
| `wayland-desktop-image` | Wayland desktop image | string | boxes | `bbbox/linux-desktop-wayland:1` | The image linux-desktop-wayland-cpu boxes run: Sway on Wayland, drawn by the CPU. setup/docker/build.sh builds it. Empty turns them off. |
| `privileged` | Docker in boxes | boolean | boxes | `true` | Give each box its own Docker daemon, started by its first docker command. Each runs as a privileged container, which can take over the Docker host. Off, or on rootless Docker, boxes say No Docker. |
| `gpu-desktops` | GPU desktops | boolean | boxes | `false` | Offer linux-desktop boxes on the host's NVIDIA GPUs, which the NVIDIA Container Toolkit lists as CDI devices (nvidia-ctk cdi generate). |
| `desktops-per-gpu` | Desktops per GPU | number | advanced | `4` | The most linux-desktop boxes that share one GPU. |
| `network` | Network | string | advanced | `bbbox` | The Docker network bb-box makes for its boxes, apart from the host's other containers. |
| `boxes` | Most boxes | number | advanced | `10` | The most bb-box containers on the host at once, running or stopped, counting those of every bb-box install that uses it. |
| `reserve-memory-mib` | Memory kept free (MiB) | number | advanced | `4096` | A new box is refused if the host would have less memory than this left, after the memory limits of the running boxes. |

### microsandbox

microsandbox: Linux boxes, with or without a desktop, as microVMs that start in under a second, on a Linux host with KVM. bb-box installs its own msb there.

Setup: [setup/microsandbox/README.md](../../setup/microsandbox/README.md).

| Field | Label | Type | Group | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `host` | Host | string | connection |  | The Linux host with KVM that runs the boxes: ssh://user@host, or bb:<machine ID> for a BB machine, which bb-box reaches through BB. Empty uses BB's server. bb-box installs its own msb there, in a folder of its own. |
| `linux-image` | Linux image | string | boxes | `bbbox/linux:1` | The image linux boxes run. bb-box imports it from Docker on the host, where setup/docker/build.sh builds it. Empty turns them off. |
| `desktop-image` | Desktop image | string | boxes | `bbbox/linux-desktop:1` | The image linux-desktop-cpu boxes run. bb-box imports it from Docker on the host, where setup/docker/build.sh builds it. Empty turns them off. |
| `linux-arm64-image` | Linux image on arm64 | string | boxes | `bbbox/linux:1-arm64` | The image linux-arm64 boxes run, on an arm64 host such as a Mac. bb-box imports it from Docker on the host, or builds it there with setup/docker/build.sh --arch arm64 in a microVM of its own. Empty turns them off. |
| `desktop-arm64-image` | Desktop image on arm64 | string | boxes | `bbbox/linux-desktop:1-arm64` | The image linux-arm64-desktop-cpu boxes run, on an arm64 host such as a Mac. bb-box imports it from Docker on the host, or builds it there in a microVM of its own. Empty turns them off. |
| `docker` | Docker in boxes | boolean | boxes | `true` | Give each box its own Docker daemon, started by its first docker command, with its data on a disk of the box's own. Each box has its own kernel, so this needs no privilege on the host. |
| `docker-disk-gib` | Docker disk (GiB) | number | advanced | `64` | The most each box's Docker disk may grow to. It takes only what Docker writes, and goes with the box. |
| `disk-gib` | Root disk (GiB) | number | advanced | `32` | The most a box's root disk may grow to when no disk size is asked for. It takes only what the box writes. |
| `network` | Network profiles | string | advanced | `public,private` | msb's network profiles for each box, comma-separated: public reaches the internet, private the host's local networks and tailnet, where BB's server often is. |
| `boxes` | Most boxes | number | advanced | `20` | The most bb-box microVMs on the host at once, running or stopped, counting those of every bb-box install that uses it. |
| `reserve-memory-mib` | Memory kept free (MiB) | number | advanced | `4096` | A new box is refused if the host would have less memory than this left, after the memory of the running boxes. |
| `memory-overcommit` | Memory overcommit | number | advanced | `1` | The boxes' memory may add up to this many times the host's, less the memory kept free. 1 counts each box at its full memory. Raise it for mostly idle boxes. |
